newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: "Dirty War" couple extradited to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: "Dirty War" couple extradited to Argentina.

text.p: A former Argentine army doctor and his wife, charged with kidnapping two children during the late 1970s "Dirty War", arrived in Argentina Thursday after being extradited from Paraguay, local news agencies said.

Former Major Norberto Atilio Bianco and his wife Susana Wehrli were arrested by Interpol in Asuncion on Monday, 10 years after charges were brought against them by the Argentine human rights group Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo.
The first extradition request was made in 1987 when Paraguay was under the dictatorship of Gen. Alfredo Stroessner.

The two children involved, Carolina, now 20, and Pablo, now 21, were brought up as Bianco's own but are suspected to be the children of Argentines killed by the military in their brutal war on suspected leftists.
Carolina and Pablo, who have both married Paraguayans, insist the Biancos are their real parents.

The Biancos are charged with forging documents and "misappropriating" minors. Their lawyer, Gilda Burgstaller, said she was optimistic because "there is not one single relative who claims paternity of the children."
The couple moved to Paraguay in the 1980s when the Grandmothers, a group made up of relatives of the tens of thousands who "disappeared", began legal action.
